Grate the gherkins coarsely and add them: Grate the gherkins coarsely and add them with a splash of their brine, then simmer for 5 minutes. Taste: it should be pleasantly sour.
Temper the soured cream with a ladle of: Temper the soured cream with a ladle of hot soup, then stir it back in off the boil. Season with pepper, salt only if needed, and lots of dill.
Season the chicken breast and cook it in: Season the chicken breast and cook it in a hot griddle pan with a little of the oil, 5 to 6 minutes a side, then let it rest.
Cut the bread into cubes and toast them: Cut the bread into cubes and toast them in a dry pan or in the oven at 200°C until crisp.
Boil the egg for 7 minutes for a jammy y: Boil the egg for 7 minutes for a jammy yolk, then cool and halve it.
Mash the anchovies with the garlic, then: Mash the anchovies with the garlic, then whisk in the yoghurt, mustard, lemon juice, the rest of the oil and half the grated parmesan.
Toss the torn lettuce with the dressing: Toss the torn lettuce with the dressing and top with the sliced chicken, croutons, egg and the rest of the parmesan.
Blitz the spring onions, chilli, garlic,: Blitz the spring onions, chilli, garlic, thyme, cinnamon, nutmeg, lime juice, sugar, salt, pepper and oil into a paste. Wear gloves if you are using scotch bonnet.
Slash the chicken and rub the paste in w: Slash the chicken and rub the paste in well. Leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Roast at 220°C or grill on a barbecue un: Roast at 220°C or grill on a barbecue until charred in places and cooked through.
Meanwhile simmer the rice with the cocon: Meanwhile simmer the rice with the coconut milk, the drained kidney beans and enough water to cover by 1 cm, with the lid on, until tender.
Serve the chicken with the rice and peas: Serve the chicken with the rice and peas and any juices from the tray.
Finely chop the parsley and garlic and m: Finely chop the parsley and garlic and mix with the oregano, chilli flakes, vinegar, salt and most of the oil. Leave it for 10 minutes for the flavours to come together.
Rub the steak with the rest of the oil,: Rub the steak with the rest of the oil, season with pepper and cook in a smoking-hot pan, 3 minutes a side for medium-rare.
Rest the steak for 5 minutes, then slice: Rest the steak for 5 minutes, then slice it.
Spoon the chimichurri over and serve wit: Spoon the chimichurri over and serve with a lettuce and tomato salad on the side.
Blitz the chilli, garlic, lemon juice, p: Blitz the chilli, garlic, lemon juice, paprika, oregano, vinegar, salt and most of the oil into a sauce.
Slash the chicken, rub it with half the: Slash the chicken, rub it with half the sauce and leave it for at least 20 minutes.
Roast at 220°C until charred at the edge: Roast at 220°C until charred at the edges and cooked through, basting halfway with a little more sauce.
Serve with the rest of the sauce and a l: Serve with the rest of the sauce and a lettuce and tomato salad dressed with the remaining oil.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clea: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then simmer it covered with 1.5 times its volume of water until the water is gone. Let it steam off the heat.
Salt the salmon and fry it skin side dow: Salt the salmon and fry it skin side down in a dry non-stick pan, turning once, until the skin is crisp and the inside just cooked.
For the soup, bring a small bowl’s worth: For the soup, bring a small bowl’s worth of water per person to a simmer and warm the cubed tofu in it.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in th: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the miso. Never boil miso once it’s in, or it turns grainy and loses its flavour.
Scatter the soup with spring onion and s: Scatter the soup with spring onion and serve it with the rice, the salmon and strips of nori for wrapping bites of rice.
Stir just-boiled water into the flour a: Stir just-boiled water into the flour a little at a time, about 50 ml per person, then knead into a smooth, soft dough. Cover and let it rest.
Roll the dough out thinly, brush it with: Roll the dough out thinly, brush it with the sesame oil and scatter over the salt and the chopped spring onion.
Roll it up like a cigar, coil it into a: Roll it up like a cigar, coil it into a snail and flatten it again into a thin round. This is what makes the flaky layers.
Fry in the oil over medium heat until go: Fry in the oil over medium heat until golden and crisp on both sides.
Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar and chil: Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar and chilli flakes for dipping, and cut the pancake into wedges.
Cook the rice: simmer it covered with 1.5 times its volume of water, then let it steam off the heat.
Beat the eggs hard with the fish sauce,: Beat the eggs hard with the fish sauce, sliced spring onion and chilli until really frothy. The air is what makes it puff.
Heat the oil in a small pan or wok until: Heat the oil in a small pan or wok until it just smokes, then pour the eggs in from a little height.
Let it puff and crisp for a minute, flip: Let it puff and crisp for a minute, flip it and give it one more minute. The edges should be lacy and golden.
Slide it onto the rice and serve with sl: Slide it onto the rice and serve with sliced cucumber and a lime wedge.
Start the rice: simmer it covered with 1: Start the rice: simmer it covered with 1.5 times its volume of water, then let it steam off the heat.
Chop the chicken finely with a knife, al: Chop the chicken finely with a knife, almost like mince. Chop the garlic and chilli together very finely.
Fry the garlic and chilli in most of the: Fry the garlic and chilli in most of the oil for 20 seconds, then add the chicken and the green beans cut short and stir-fry over high heat.
Add the soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar: Add the soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar with a splash of water, toss until glossy, then stir in the basil leaves until they wilt.
Fry the egg in the rest of the oil in a: Fry the egg in the rest of the oil in a very hot pan until the edges are crisp and the yolk still runny. Serve it on the rice with the chicken.
Bring a pot of water to the boil with ha: Bring a pot of water to the boil with half the ginger in slices, the spring onion and the salt. Add the chicken, bring back to a bare simmer, cover and poach gently.
Lift the chicken into a bowl of iced wat: Lift the chicken into a bowl of iced water for a few minutes. This keeps it silky and tightens the skin. Keep the broth.
Fry the rinsed rice with half the garlic: Fry the rinsed rice with half the garlic, grated, in the sesame oil, then cook it in 1.5 times its volume of the broth until fluffy.
For the chilli sauce, blitz or pound the: For the chilli sauce, blitz or pound the chilli with the rest of the ginger and garlic, a squeeze of lime and a spoon of broth.
Slice the chicken, drizzle it with the s: Slice the chicken, drizzle it with the soy sauce and serve with the rice, sliced cucumber, the chilli sauce and a small cup of the hot broth.
Put the chicken in a pan with the soy sa: Put the chicken in a pan with the soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, bay leaf and cracked black pepper and leave it to marinate.
Add a splash of water, bring to the boil: Add a splash of water, bring to the boil and simmer uncovered. Don’t stir at first, so the sharp edge of the vinegar cooks off.
Meanwhile cook the rice: simmer it cover: Meanwhile cook the rice: simmer it covered with 1.5 times its volume of water, then let it steam off the heat.
Lift out the chicken and brown it in the: Lift out the chicken and brown it in the oil in a hot frying pan until the skin crisps.
Stir the sugar into the sauce and boil i: Stir the sugar into the sauce and boil it down until glossy, then pour it over the chicken and serve with the rice.
Cut the chicken into large bite-size pie: Cut the chicken into large bite-size pieces, season with the salt and grated ginger, then toss with the flour and a splash of cold water until each piece has a thin coat of batter.
Heat the oil about 2 cm deep in a small: Heat the oil about 2 cm deep in a small pan to 170°C and fry the chicken in batches until pale golden. Let it rest on a rack.
Fry it a second time in hotter oil until: Fry it a second time in hotter oil until deep golden and shatteringly crisp. The double fry is the secret.
Bubble the gochujang, honey, soy sauce a: Bubble the gochujang, honey, soy sauce and grated garlic with a spoon of water until glossy.
Toss the hot chicken in the sauce, scatt: Toss the hot chicken in the sauce, scatter with sesame seeds and serve straight away with the rice.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clea: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then simmer it covered with 1.2 times its volume of water and let it steam off the heat for 10 minutes.
Stir the vinegar, sugar and salt until d: Stir the vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved and fold it into the hot rice with a cutting motion. Spread it out to cool to room temperature.
Cut the salmon, cucumber and avocado int: Cut the salmon, cucumber and avocado into long thin strips. Use sushi-grade salmon, or salmon frozen for at least 24 hours first.
Lay a nori sheet shiny side down on a ba: Lay a nori sheet shiny side down on a bamboo mat or cling film. With wet hands, spread a thin layer of rice over it, leaving a 2 cm strip bare at the top.
Lay a line of filling across the bottom,: Lay a line of filling across the bottom, then roll it up firmly, pressing as you go. Dab the bare edge with water to seal.
Cut each roll into 6 to 8 pieces with a: Cut each roll into 6 to 8 pieces with a sharp, wet knife and serve with the soy sauce.
Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes and slip th: Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes and slip them into gently simmering water. It firms them up so they don’t break in the sauce.
Fry the pork mince in the oil until cris: Fry the pork mince in the oil until crisp and brown, then add the garlic, ginger, chilli flakes and miso and fry for a minute until the oil turns red.
Add the soy sauce and a small cup of wat: Add the soy sauce and a small cup of water, slide in the drained tofu and simmer, nudging the pan rather than stirring.
Grind over plenty of pepper, scatter wit: Grind over plenty of pepper, scatter with spring onion and serve over the rice.
Bring the stock to the boil with the sli: Bring the stock to the boil with the sliced mushrooms and the carrot cut into thin matchsticks.
Add the tofu cut into thin strips, the s: Add the tofu cut into thin strips, the soy sauce, vinegar, plenty of pepper and the chilli flakes. Taste: it should be properly sour and peppery.
Mix the flour with a splash of cold wate: Mix the flour with a splash of cold water, stir it in and simmer until the soup thickens slightly.
Stir the soup in one direction and slowl: Stir the soup in one direction and slowly pour in the beaten egg so it sets in silky ribbons.
Finish with a few drops of sesame oil an: Finish with a few drops of sesame oil and the sliced spring onion.
Cut the tofu into slices about 1 cm thic: Cut the tofu into slices about 1 cm thick and pat them very dry with kitchen paper.
Fry the slices in the oil over medium-hi: Fry the slices in the oil over medium-high heat until golden on both sides.
Mix the soy sauce, chilli flakes, choppe: Mix the soy sauce, chilli flakes, chopped garlic, sugar, half the spring onion and a few spoons of water, and pour it over the tofu.
Simmer, spooning the sauce over, until i: Simmer, spooning the sauce over, until it is almost all soaked up. Finish with the sesame oil, sesame seeds and the rest of the spring onion and serve with the rice.
Season the chicken and brown it well in: Season the chicken and brown it well in the oil, skin side first. Lift it out.
Soften the sliced onion, pepper and mush: Soften the sliced onion, pepper and mushrooms in the same pan, then add the garlic and rosemary.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble away: Pour in the wine and let it bubble away by half, scraping up the brown bits.
Add the tomatoes and olives, nestle the: Add the tomatoes and olives, nestle the chicken back in and simmer half covered until the chicken is tender and the sauce thick. It’s even better the next day.
Bring the stock to a simmer and drop in: Bring the stock to a simmer and drop in the spinach for a minute.
Beat the eggs with the grated parmesan,: Beat the eggs with the grated parmesan, nutmeg and a little salt and pepper.
Stir the soup in a slow circle and pour: Stir the soup in a slow circle and pour in the egg mixture in a thin stream. Wait 30 seconds, then break it up gently with a fork into soft shreds.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and serve: Finish with a squeeze of lemon and serve straight away.
Bring a big pot of salted water to the b: Bring a big pot of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta.
Two minutes before the end, add the aspa: Two minutes before the end, add the asparagus cut into short pieces and the peas to the same pot.
Meanwhile soften the sliced garlic and d: Meanwhile soften the sliced garlic and diced courgette in the oil, then add the halved cherry tomatoes until they just start to burst.
Drain the pasta and vegetables, keeping: Drain the pasta and vegetables, keeping a cup of the water. Toss everything in the pan with the parmesan, lemon zest and juice and a splash of pasta water until glossy.
Finish with torn basil and black pepper.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Halve the courge: Heat the oven to 200°C. Halve the courgettes lengthways, scoop out the middles with a teaspoon and chop the scooped flesh.
Fry the onion and the chopped courgette: Fry the onion and the chopped courgette flesh in half the oil, then add the mince and brown it.
Off the heat, mix in the egg, most of th: Off the heat, mix in the egg, most of the parmesan, half the breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.
Spread the tomatoes with the crushed gar: Spread the tomatoes with the crushed garlic in a baking dish, set the courgette boats on top and fill them generously.
Top with the rest of the breadcrumbs and: Top with the rest of the breadcrumbs and parmesan, drizzle with the rest of the oil and bake until golden.
Cut the aubergine into 2 cm cubes, toss: Cut the aubergine into 2 cm cubes, toss with the salt and leave in a colander.
Pat the aubergine dry and fry it in most: Pat the aubergine dry and fry it in most of the oil until golden and soft. Lift it out.
In the same pan soften the onion and cel: In the same pan soften the onion and celery, then add the tomatoes and simmer.
Stir in the olives, capers, raisins, vin: Stir in the olives, capers, raisins, vinegar and sugar, fold the aubergine back in and simmer until thick and glossy.
Toast the pine nuts and scatter them ove: Toast the pine nuts and scatter them over with torn basil. Let it cool a little: Sicilians eat it warm or at room temperature.
Stir the grated garlic and the salt into: Stir the grated garlic and the salt into the yoghurt and let it come to room temperature.
Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer: Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer with the vinegar. Crack each egg into a cup, swirl the water and slide them in to poach.
Melt the butter until foaming and nutty,: Melt the butter until foaming and nutty, then stir in the chilli flakes and paprika.
Spread the yoghurt on a plate, set the e: Spread the yoghurt on a plate, set the eggs on top, pour over the red butter and finish with dill. Serve with bread to mop it all up.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil unti: Soften the chopped onion in the oil until sweet.
Add the spinach a handful at a time with: Add the spinach a handful at a time with the salt and let it wilt, then cook off the liquid.
Make a hollow for each egg, crack them i: Make a hollow for each egg, crack them in, cover and cook on low heat until the whites set and the yolks are still soft.
Scatter with chilli flakes and serve wit: Scatter with chilli flakes and serve with spoonfuls of yoghurt.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Cut the potatoes: Heat the oven to 190°C. Cut the potatoes, courgette, aubergine, pepper and onion into chunky pieces and put them in a roasting tin.
Grate the tomatoes, throw away the skins: Grate the tomatoes, throw away the skins and mix the pulp with the crushed garlic, oregano, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Pour it over the vegetables, toss well a: Pour it over the vegetables, toss well and add a small glass of water to the tin. Cover with foil and bake.
Uncover, stir gently and roast until the: Uncover, stir gently and roast until the vegetables are soft and caramelised at the edges.
Let it rest and finish with parsley. Bri: Let it rest and finish with parsley. Briam is even better warm than hot.
Grate the onion and mix half of it with: Grate the onion and mix half of it with the mince, parsley, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper. Knead for a couple of minutes until sticky.
Shape into small fingers and chill them: Shape into small fingers and chill them while you make the pilaf.
Soften the rest of the onion in half the: Soften the rest of the onion in half the oil, stir in the tomato purée, then add the bulgur and stock. Cover and cook on low heat.
Fry or grill the köfte in the rest of th: Fry or grill the köfte in the rest of the oil until browned and just cooked through.
Fluff up the pilaf and serve it with the: Fluff up the pilaf and serve it with the köfte, the yoghurt and diced cucumber.
Prick the aubergine a few times and char: Prick the aubergine a few times and char it over a gas flame or under a very hot grill, turning, until the skin is black and the inside collapses.
Let it cool in a colander so the bitter: Let it cool in a colander so the bitter juices drain, then scoop out the smoky flesh.
Mash it with a fork with the tahini, cru: Mash it with a fork with the tahini, crushed garlic, lemon juice and salt. Don’t blend it smooth; it should stay a little rough.
Spread it on a plate, make a swirl, driz: Spread it on a plate, make a swirl, drizzle with the oil and scatter over parsley and pomegranate seeds.
Warm the pitta and serve with cucumber s: Warm the pitta and serve with cucumber sticks for dipping.
Cut the lamb into big chunks and rub the: Cut the lamb into big chunks and rub them with the cumin, cinnamon, grated ginger, salt and pepper.
Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot, then add the sliced onions and cook until soft.
Pour in the stock, cover and simmer very: Pour in the stock, cover and simmer very gently until the lamb is meltingly tender.
Stir in the raisins and honey and cook u: Stir in the raisins and honey and cook uncovered until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Pour boiling water over the couscous, co: Pour boiling water over the couscous, cover for five minutes and fluff with a fork. Serve the tagine on top with toasted almonds and coriander.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fra: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, then grind them finely.
Brown the chicken in the oil, then softe: Brown the chicken in the oil, then soften the chopped onion with the turmeric and cinnamon in the same pot.
Add the walnuts and a mug of water per p: Add the walnuts and a mug of water per person, then the juice squeezed from the pomegranate seeds (save a few seeds), the lemon juice, sugar and salt.
Simmer very gently, stirring now and the: Simmer very gently, stirring now and then, until the sauce is dark and thick and the walnut oil rises to the top. Taste: it should be both sweet and sour.
Cook the rice: simmer it covered with 1.5 times its volume of water, then let it steam off the heat. Serve the fesenjan over it with the saved pomegranate seeds.
Put the chicken in a pot with the choppe: Put the chicken in a pot with the chopped onion, ginger, saffron, a little of the cinnamon, the salt and a mug of water. Cover and simmer until very tender.
Lift out the chicken and shred it. Boil: Lift out the chicken and shred it. Boil the liquid down to a few spoonfuls, then stir in the beaten eggs over low heat until softly set. Add the parsley and the chicken.
Toast the almonds, chop them and mix wit: Toast the almonds, chop them and mix with most of the sugar and cinnamon.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Brush a tin with: Heat the oven to 190°C. Brush a tin with melted butter and line it with overlapping filo sheets, buttering each one and leaving plenty hanging over the sides.
Layer in the almonds and then the chicke: Layer in the almonds and then the chicken, fold the overhanging filo over, top with two more buttered sheets and tuck in the edges.
Bake until deep golden, then dust with t: Bake until deep golden, then dust with the last of the sugar and cinnamon in a criss-cross pattern.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil unti: Soften the chopped onion in the oil until sweet, then add the garlic.
Add the trimmed beans and the potatoes c: Add the trimmed beans and the potatoes cut into chunks and stir to coat them in the oil.
Add the tomatoes, the salt and just enou: Add the tomatoes, the salt and just enough water to come halfway up. Cover and simmer gently until the beans are very soft and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the dill and let it rest. Greeks: Stir in the dill and let it rest. Greeks eat it warm, never piping hot.
Fry the cumin in the oil for a few secon: Fry the cumin in the oil for a few seconds until it crackles, then add the chopped onion and green chilli and soften.
Add the chopped tomato, turmeric, garam: Add the chopped tomato, turmeric, garam masala and salt and cook until the tomato collapses.
Crumble the tofu in with your hands and: Crumble the tofu in with your hands and fry, stirring, until hot and a little dry, like scrambled eggs.
Fold in the spinach until it wilts, then: Fold in the spinach until it wilts, then finish with coriander.
Fry the cumin in the oil until it crackl: Fry the cumin in the oil until it crackles, then add the chopped onion and cook slowly until deep golden.
Add the grated ginger, garlic and chilli: Add the grated ginger, garlic and chilli for a minute, then the chopped tomatoes, turmeric, garam masala and salt. Cook down into a thick masala.
Add the drained beans and a small glass: Add the drained beans and a small glass of water per person and simmer. Mash a few beans against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
Scatter the rajma with coriander and ser: Scatter the rajma with coriander and serve it over the rice.
Mix half the yoghurt with the garam masa: Mix half the yoghurt with the garam masala, paprika, turmeric, grated ginger and garlic, half the lemon juice, the oil and the salt.
Cut the paneer, pepper and red onion int: Cut the paneer, pepper and red onion into large chunks, coat them in the marinade and leave for at least 20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill or roast a: Thread onto skewers and grill or roast at 230°C, turning once, until charred at the edges.
Stir the chopped mint and grated cucumbe: Stir the chopped mint and grated cucumber into the rest of the yoghurt with the rest of the lemon and serve it with the tikka.
Boil the potatoes until tender, drain we: Boil the potatoes until tender, drain well and let them steam dry.
Mash the potatoes with the grated paneer: Mash the potatoes with the grated paneer, chickpea flour and half the salt into a smooth dough, then roll into balls with a piece of cashew hidden in each.
Fry the koftas in hot oil, turning, unti: Fry the koftas in hot oil, turning, until golden all over. Drain them on kitchen paper.
For the sauce, soften the onion with the: For the sauce, soften the onion with the ginger, add the tomatoes, garam masala, chilli flakes, the rest of the salt and the rest of the cashews, simmer, then blend until velvety.
Stir in the cream and sugar and simmer f: Stir in the cream and sugar and simmer for a minute.
Cook the rice: simmer it covered with 1.5 times its volume of water, then let it steam off the heat. Pour the hot sauce over the koftas just before serving so they stay whole.
Toast the cumin in a dry pan until it sm: Toast the cumin in a dry pan until it smells nutty, then crush it.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas and toss t: Drain and rinse the chickpeas and toss them with the diced cucumber, tomato and red onion.
Add the chopped chilli, coriander and mi: Add the chopped chilli, coriander and mint, the toasted cumin, the lime juice and salt, and mix well.
Let it sit for five minutes so the chick: Let it sit for five minutes so the chickpeas soak up the tangy juices, then taste and add more lime if needed.
Soften the onion, garlic and chilli in a: Soften the onion, garlic and chilli in a little of the oil, add the tomatoes and salt and simmer into a loose salsa.
Slice the plantain and fry it in a littl: Slice the plantain and fry it in a little more oil until caramelised on both sides.
Warm the black beans with a splash of wa: Warm the black beans with a splash of water and mash them roughly. Warm the peas in the salsa.
Crisp the tortillas in the pan, spread t: Crisp the tortillas in the pan, spread them with the beans, then fry the eggs in the rest of the oil.
Put an egg on each tortilla, spoon over: Put an egg on each tortilla, spoon over the salsa with the peas, crumble over the cheese and serve with the plantain.
Mix the lime juice with the crushed garl: Mix the lime juice with the crushed garlic, cumin, oil, salt and pepper and coat the steak in it. Leave it for 30 minutes.
Cook the steak in a smoking hot pan or o: Cook the steak in a smoking hot pan or on a barbecue, about 3 minutes a side, then let it rest.
Mash the avocado with a pinch of salt an: Mash the avocado with a pinch of salt and finely chop the onion, coriander and chilli.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, slice t: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, slice the steak thinly across the grain and pile it in with the avocado, onion, coriander and chilli.
Brown the mince in the oil, breaking it: Brown the mince in the oil, breaking it up, until it crisps a little.
Add the onion, garlic and cumin and fry: Add the onion, garlic and cumin and fry until soft.
Stir in the tomatoes with the potato and: Stir in the tomatoes with the potato and carrot cut into small cubes, season and add a splash of water. Cover and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Add the peas for the last few minutes an: Add the peas for the last few minutes and serve with the rice.
Fry the diced bacon and chorizo until th: Fry the diced bacon and chorizo until the fat runs and they crisp.
Add the onion, garlic and chilli and sof: Add the onion, garlic and chilli and soften them in the fat, then add the chopped tomato.
Add the drained beans and the stock and: Add the drained beans and the stock and simmer gently so the smoky flavours soak into the beans.
Season with salt, stir in the coriander: Season with salt, stir in the coriander and serve in bowls with warm tortillas.
Char the peppers under a hot grill or ov: Char the peppers under a hot grill or over a flame, turning, until black all over. Seal them in a bowl to sweat, then peel, slit open and remove the seeds.
For the walnut sauce, soak the walnuts i: For the walnut sauce, soak the walnuts in the milk, then blend with the cheese, sugar and a pinch of salt until smooth and pourable.
Fry the onion in the oil, add both mince: Fry the onion in the oil, add both minces and brown them, then add the chopped tomato, apple, raisins, chopped almonds and cinnamon. Simmer until thick.
Stuff the peppers with the filling and l: Stuff the peppers with the filling and lay them on plates. They’re served warm or at room temperature, not hot.
Pour the cold walnut sauce over and fini: Pour the cold walnut sauce over and finish with pomegranate seeds and parsley: the green, white and red of the Mexican flag.
Toast the thin pasta in half the oil in: Toast the thin pasta in half the oil in a wide pan, stirring, until golden brown. Tip it out.
Fry the squid rings and prawns quickly i: Fry the squid rings and prawns quickly in the rest of the oil and lift out the prawns.
Add most of the garlic, the paprika and: Add most of the garlic, the paprika and the grated tomato and cook into a thick sofrito.
Pour in the hot stock with the saffron a: Pour in the hot stock with the saffron and salt, bring to the boil and add the pasta. Cook without stirring until the stock is absorbed.
Lay the prawns on top and put the pan un: Lay the prawns on top and put the pan under a hot grill until the noodles curl up and crisp at the ends.
Let it rest for a few minutes and serve: Let it rest for a few minutes and serve with the mayonnaise mixed with the last of the garlic, alioli style, and a lemon wedge.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Slice the tomato and red onion and dress: Slice the tomato and red onion and dress them with half the oil and a pinch of salt.
Pat the sardines dry, salt them and cook: Pat the sardines dry, salt them and cook them on a very hot griddle or pan, about 2 minutes a side, until charred.
Mix the rest of the oil with the chopped: Mix the rest of the oil with the chopped garlic and parsley, spoon it over the sardines and potatoes and serve with lemon.
Boil the potatoes in their skins in salt: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water, adding the eggs for the last 10 minutes.
Cool the eggs in cold water. Peel the po: Cool the eggs in cold water. Peel the potatoes and cut them into chunks while still warm.
Dress the warm potatoes with the oil, vi: Dress the warm potatoes with the oil, vinegar and a pinch of salt so they soak up the flavour.
Add the diced pepper, tomato and red oni: Add the diced pepper, tomato and red onion, the olives and the tuna, then top with the quartered eggs. It’s even better after an hour in the fridge.
Cook the sliced onions and peppers very: Cook the sliced onions and peppers very slowly in the oil with the garlic until soft and sweet.
Add the paprika and tomatoes and simmer,: Add the paprika and tomatoes and simmer, then blend into a smooth, brick-red sauce.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted wa: Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Season the cod, lay it in the sauce, cov: Season the cod, lay it in the sauce, cover and cook gently until it just flakes. Serve with the potatoes.
Whisk the chia seeds with the oat milk,: Whisk the chia seeds with the oat milk, coconut milk and maple syrup, then whisk again after a minute so no clumps form.
Leave it in the fridge until thick and s: Leave it in the fridge until thick and spoonable, or overnight.
Mash or blend half the mango into a puré: Mash or blend half the mango into a purée and dice the rest.
Layer the pudding with the mango purée i: Layer the pudding with the mango purée in a glass and top with the diced mango.

Blend until silky smooth, season with th: Blend until silky smooth, season with the salt, pepper and a little grated nutmeg and serve.
Heat the oven to 220°C with the butter i: Heat the oven to 220°C with the butter in an ovenproof frying pan or dish.
Whisk the eggs, flour, milk and half the: Whisk the eggs, flour, milk and half the sugar into a smooth batter and let it rest while the oven heats.
When the butter is sizzling, pour in the: When the butter is sizzling, pour in the batter and bake without opening the door until puffed and deep golden.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, dust with: Squeeze over the lemon juice, dust with the rest of the sugar and pile on the berries. Eat it straight away, before it sinks.
Stir in the buttermilk to a shaggy dough: Stir in the buttermilk to a shaggy dough, pat it out 2 cm thick, fold it over twice and cut out thick rounds.
Bake the biscuits until tall and golden.
Meanwhile squeeze the sausage meat out o: Meanwhile squeeze the sausage meat out of the skins and fry it, breaking it up, until browned.
Sprinkle over the rest of the flour, sti: Sprinkle over the rest of the flour, stir for a minute, then pour in the milk and simmer, stirring, into a thick gravy. Season with lots of black pepper.
Split the warm biscuits and spoon the gr: Split the warm biscuits and spoon the gravy over.
Heat the oven to 175°C and line a loaf t: Heat the oven to 175°C and line a loaf tin with baking paper.
Mash the very ripe bananas, then beat in: Mash the very ripe bananas, then beat in the melted butter, sugar and egg.
Scrape into the tin and bake until a ske: Scrape into the tin and bake until a skewer comes out clean.
Let it cool in the tin for 10 minutes be: Let it cool in the tin for 10 minutes before slicing.
Blend the cottage cheese, oats, egg, ban: Blend the cottage cheese, oats, egg, banana and cinnamon into a thick batter and let it stand for 2 minutes.
Wipe a non-stick pan with the butter and: Wipe a non-stick pan with the butter and cook small pancakes over medium heat until bubbles appear, then flip them.
Serve stacked with the berries and a dri: Serve stacked with the berries and a drizzle of maple syrup.
Warm most of the oil in a big pot and so: Warm most of the oil in a big pot and soften the onion, leek and one garlic clove, all sliced, without browning.
Add the chopped tomato, saffron, thinly: Add the chopped tomato, saffron, thinly sliced potatoes and the stock and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Season with the salt, then add the cod i: Season with the salt, then add the cod in chunks and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Add the mussels and prawns, cover and co: Add the mussels and prawns, cover and cook until the mussels open. Throw away any that stay shut.
Toast the bread, rub it with the other g: Toast the bread, rub it with the other garlic clove, drizzle with the rest of the oil and ladle the soup over it.
Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water: Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water. After 10 minutes, lay the chopped kale on top, cover and cook together until the potatoes are soft.
Meanwhile fry the sausages until browned: Meanwhile fry the sausages until browned and hot all the way through.
Drain, then mash the potatoes and kale w: Drain, then mash the potatoes and kale with the warm milk and butter until rough and creamy. Season with pepper.
Serve the mash with the sliced sausage o: Serve the mash with the sliced sausage on top and mustard on the side. Make a little well in the mash for gravy or a knob of butter, the Dutch way.
Bring the milk and the same amount of wa: Bring the milk and the same amount of water to the boil with the salt, whisk in the polenta and cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir the cheddar and half the butter int: Stir the cheddar and half the butter into the grits, cover and keep warm.
Fry the bacon in small pieces until cris: Fry the bacon in small pieces until crisp, then lift it out and leave the fat in the pan.
Toss the prawns with the paprika and fry: Toss the prawns with the paprika and fry them in the bacon fat with the chopped garlic until just pink, then add the rest of the butter and a squeeze of lemon.
Spoon the prawns over the grits and top: Spoon the prawns over the grits and top with the bacon and sliced spring onion.
Boil the sweet potato in thick slices an: Boil the sweet potato in thick slices and the sweetcorn until tender, then let them cool.
Slice the red onion very thinly and rins: Slice the red onion very thinly and rinse it in cold water so it's crisp and mild.
Cut the hake into bite-sized cubes (use: Cut the hake into bite-sized cubes (use very fresh fish that has been frozen first), season with the salt and chopped chilli, then squeeze over the lime juice to cover.
Leave it for 5 minutes, just until the o: Leave it for 5 minutes, just until the outside turns white. The inside should stay soft.
Toss in the onion and coriander and serv: Toss in the onion and coriander and serve at once on lettuce, with the sweet potato and corn.
Blend the red pepper, crushed tomato, ha: Blend the red pepper, crushed tomato, half the onion, the chilli, garlic and ginger until smooth.
Fry the rest of the onion, sliced, in th: Fry the rest of the onion, sliced, in the oil until soft, then stir in the tomato puree and fry it for 2 minutes until it darkens.
Pour in the blended sauce with the thyme: Pour in the blended sauce with the thyme, curry powder, bay leaf and salt and cook it down until thick and the oil rises to the top.
Stir in the washed rice and the stock, c: Stir in the washed rice and the stock, cover tightly with foil and a lid and cook on the lowest heat without stirring.
Turn off the heat and let it steam for 5: Turn off the heat and let it steam for 5 minutes, then fluff it up with a fork. A little crust at the bottom is the prize.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the sweet p: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the sweet potato cubes and chickpeas with the oil, cumin and salt and roast until golden.
Meanwhile rinse the quinoa and simmer it: Meanwhile rinse the quinoa and simmer it in twice its volume of water until the water is absorbed.
Massage the shredded kale with a squeeze: Massage the shredded kale with a squeeze of the lemon for a minute so it softens.
Whisk the tahini with the rest of the le: Whisk the tahini with the rest of the lemon juice and a little water into a pourable dressing.
Build the bowls with the quinoa, kale, r: Build the bowls with the quinoa, kale, roasted sweet potato and chickpeas and shredded red cabbage, then drizzle with the dressing.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clea: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then simmer it covered with a little more water than rice and let it steam off the heat. Short-grain rice holds together best.
Mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise: Mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise and soy sauce.
Wet your hands, rub them with a little s: Wet your hands, rub them with a little salt and flatten a handful of warm rice in your palm. Put a spoon of tuna in the middle, close the rice around it and press it into a firm triangle.
Wrap a strip of nori around the bottom o: Wrap a strip of nori around the bottom of each onigiri and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Rinse the rice, then simmer it in about: Rinse the rice, then simmer it in about four times its volume of water, stirring often, until the grains burst and it turns creamy. Sticky or short-grain rice gives the silkiest result.
Whisk the cocoa with a splash of hot wat: Whisk the cocoa with a splash of hot water until smooth, then stir it into the rice with the sugar and salt. Simmer until thick like porridge: it thickens more as it cools.
Spoon into bowls and swirl the milk over: Spoon into bowls and swirl the milk over the top.
Char the halved onion and the sliced gin: Char the halved onion and the sliced ginger in a dry pan until blackened in spots. This gives pho its smoky depth.
Put them in a pot with the stock, star a: Put them in a pot with the stock, star anise, cinnamon and chicken thighs. Bring to a bare simmer, skim, and cook gently so the broth stays clear.
Lift out the chicken and shred it. Strai: Lift out the chicken and shred it. Strain the broth and season it with the fish sauce.
Soak or cook the rice noodles as the pac: Soak or cook the rice noodles as the packet says and divide them between deep bowls.
Top with the chicken, pour over the boil: Top with the chicken, pour over the boiling broth and finish with beansprouts, coriander, sliced spring onion, chilli and a squeeze of lime.
Bash the lemongrass with a rolling pin a: Bash the lemongrass with a rolling pin and cut it into short lengths. Slice the ginger thinly (use galangal if you can find it).
Bring the stock and coconut milk to a ge: Bring the stock and coconut milk to a gentle simmer with the lemongrass and ginger. Don’t let it boil hard or the coconut milk splits.
Add the sliced chicken and mushrooms and: Add the sliced chicken and mushrooms and poach until the chicken is cooked through.
Off the heat, season with the fish sauce: Off the heat, season with the fish sauce, sugar and lime juice. It should taste sour, salty and creamy all at once.
Serve topped with coriander and sliced c: Serve topped with coriander and sliced chilli. The lemongrass is there for flavour, not for eating.
Cut the chicken into strips and marinate: Cut the chicken into strips and marinate it with the crushed garlic, turmeric, half the soy sauce, the sugar and the oil.
Thread the chicken onto skewers and gril: Thread the chicken onto skewers and grill or griddle on high heat until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Warm the peanut butter with the coconut: Warm the peanut butter with the coconut milk, the rest of the soy sauce, half the lime juice and the chilli flakes, stirring until smooth and glossy.
Serve the skewers with the rice, sliced: Serve the skewers with the rice, sliced cucumber, the peanut sauce and the rest of the lime.
Blanch the spinach and beansprouts for a: Blanch the spinach and beansprouts for a minute, squeeze dry and season each with a few drops of sesame oil and a little of the garlic.
Stir-fry the carrot and courgette matchs: Stir-fry the carrot and courgette matchsticks separately in a little oil, just until bright.
Fry the mince with the soy sauce, sugar: Fry the mince with the soy sauce, sugar and the rest of the garlic until browned and sticky.
Fry the egg sunny side up.
Fill bowls with rice, arrange everything: Fill bowls with rice, arrange everything in neat piles on top with the egg in the middle, add a spoon of gochujang and the sesame seeds, then mix it all up at the table.
Soften the chopped onion, carrot and dic: Soften the chopped onion, carrot and diced potato in a third of the oil.
Stir in the curry powder and a spoon of: Stir in the curry powder and a spoon of the flour, cook for a minute, then whisk in the stock with the honey and soy sauce. Simmer until the potato is tender and the sauce is thick.
Flatten the chicken to an even thickness: Flatten the chicken to an even thickness and season it. Dip it in the rest of the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs, pressing them on well.
Shallow-fry it in the rest of the oil un: Shallow-fry it in the rest of the oil until golden and cooked through. Rest it for a minute, slice, and serve on the rice with the curry sauce alongside.
Cook the noodles for a minute less than: Cook the noodles for a minute less than the packet says, then drain and rinse them briefly so they don’t stick.
Fry the thinly sliced pork belly in a ho: Fry the thinly sliced pork belly in a hot pan with the oil until it renders and crisps.
Add the sliced onion, carrot, pepper and: Add the sliced onion, carrot, pepper and cabbage and stir-fry on high heat until just tender.
Toss in the noodles with the soy sauce a: Toss in the noodles with the soy sauce and barbecue sauce, standing in for yakisoba sauce, until coated and catching in places. Serve with sliced spring onion.
Fry the curry paste and crushed garlic i: Fry the curry paste and crushed garlic in a splash of the coconut milk until fragrant and the oil starts to separate.
Pour in the stock and the rest of the co: Pour in the stock and the rest of the coconut milk, season with the fish sauce and sugar, and simmer.
Add the tofu cubes and the prawns and po: Add the tofu cubes and the prawns and poach until the prawns turn pink.
Meanwhile soak the rice noodles in boili: Meanwhile soak the rice noodles in boiling water until soft, drain and divide them between bowls.
Ladle the soup over and top with beanspr: Ladle the soup over and top with beansprouts, sliced chilli, coriander and a wedge of lime.
Put the pasta on to boil in well-salted: Put the pasta on to boil in well-salted water.
Warm the oil with the sliced garlic, chi: Warm the oil with the sliced garlic, chilli flakes and anchovies, stirring until the anchovies melt into the oil.
Add the tomatoes, olives and capers and: Add the tomatoes, olives and capers and simmer briskly until thickened.
Toss the drained pasta in the sauce with: Toss the drained pasta in the sauce with a splash of its cooking water and finish with parsley. No cheese needed: it’s salty enough.
Cut the aubergine into cubes, salt them: Cut the aubergine into cubes, salt them lightly and leave them to sweat, then pat dry.
Fry the aubergine in most of the oil unt: Fry the aubergine in most of the oil until deep golden and soft.
In another pan, warm the rest of the oil: In another pan, warm the rest of the oil with the sliced garlic, add the tomatoes and simmer into a thick sauce.
Boil the pasta, drain, and toss it with: Boil the pasta, drain, and toss it with the sauce, half the aubergine and torn basil.
Serve with the rest of the aubergine on: Serve with the rest of the aubergine on top and the ricotta crumbled over.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Simmer the tomat: Heat the oven to 200°C. Simmer the tomatoes with the crushed garlic, oregano and a pinch of salt into a thick sauce.
Slice the chicken breast in half horizon: Slice the chicken breast in half horizontally and flatten it. Coat it in flour, then beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs mixed with half the parmesan.
Fry in the oil until golden on both side: Fry in the oil until golden on both sides.
Lay the chicken in a baking dish, spoon: Lay the chicken in a baking dish, spoon over the sauce, cover with torn mozzarella and the rest of the parmesan, and bake until bubbling.
Scatter with basil and serve with a gree: Scatter with basil and serve with a green salad.
Soften the chopped onion in the butter,: Soften the chopped onion in the butter, add the rice and stir for a minute. Add the hot stock with the saffron a ladle at a time, stirring, until the rice is cooked and very thick.
Stir in the parmesan, spread the risotto: Stir in the parmesan, spread the risotto on a tray and let it cool completely. It has to be cold to shape.
Simmer the tomatoes with the peas and a: Simmer the tomatoes with the peas and a pinch of salt into a thick little ragù.
Wet your hands, flatten a ball of rice i: Wet your hands, flatten a ball of rice in your palm, add a spoon of the filling and a cube of mozzarella, then close it into a ball.
Roll each ball in flour, then beaten egg: Roll each ball in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil, turning, until deep gold: Fry in hot oil, turning, until deep golden all over. Drain on kitchen paper and rest for a few minutes: the middle is molten.
Soak the saffron in a splash of hot wate: Soak the saffron in a splash of hot water and the raisins in another.
Toast the breadcrumbs in a little of the: Toast the breadcrumbs in a little of the oil until golden and crunchy, then set them aside.
Soften the finely chopped onion in the r: Soften the finely chopped onion in the rest of the oil.
Add the sardines, breaking them up, then: Add the sardines, breaking them up, then the drained raisins, the pine nuts and the saffron water. Cook gently for a few minutes.
Boil the pasta in salted water and toss: Boil the pasta in salted water and toss it with the sauce and a little cooking water. Finish with the dill (standing in for wild fennel), the parsley and the crunchy breadcrumbs.
Warm the flatbread in a dry pan for a mi: Warm the flatbread in a dry pan for a minute on each side.
Lay the sliced mozzarella over one half: Lay the sliced mozzarella over one half and let it start to melt.
Add the ham, sliced tomato and lettuce,: Add the ham, sliced tomato and lettuce, fold it over and press down for a moment. Cut in half and eat warm.
Brown the sausages all over in the oil,: Brown the sausages all over in the oil, then take them out.
In the same pan, soften the finely chopp: In the same pan, soften the finely chopped onion, carrot and celery with the garlic and rosemary.
Add the rinsed lentils, the tomatoes and: Add the rinsed lentils, the tomatoes and the stock, put the sausages back and simmer until the lentils are tender and most of the liquid has gone.
Season with salt and serve in warm bowls: Season with salt and serve in warm bowls.
Hard-boil the egg, cool it in cold water: Hard-boil the egg, cool it in cold water and slice it.
Slice the aubergine into rounds, brush t: Slice the aubergine into rounds, brush them with the oil, salt them and fry or roast until soft and browned.
Chop the cucumber, tomato and parsley in: Chop the cucumber, tomato and parsley into a small salad.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice an: Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice and enough cold water to make a pourable sauce.
Warm the pitta, open it up and layer the: Warm the pitta, open it up and layer the aubergine, egg and salad inside, with tahini sauce on every layer.
Cut the pork into cubes and marinate wit: Cut the pork into cubes and marinate with half the oil, the lemon juice, oregano, half the garlic and the salt.
For the tzatziki, grate the cucumber, sq: For the tzatziki, grate the cucumber, squeeze out the water and mix it with the yoghurt, the rest of the garlic and the rest of the oil.
Thread the pork onto skewers and grill o: Thread the pork onto skewers and grill on high heat, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Warm the pitta and fill it with the pork: Warm the pitta and fill it with the pork, tzatziki, sliced tomato and red onion.
Simmer the chicken in the stock with the: Simmer the chicken in the stock with the chopped onion and carrot until cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and shred it. Add t: Lift out the chicken and shred it. Add the rice to the pot and simmer until tender.
Whisk the egg with the lemon juice until: Whisk the egg with the lemon juice until frothy, then slowly whisk in a ladle of the hot broth to warm it.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in th: Take the pot off the heat and stir in the egg mixture: the soup turns silky and pale. Don’t let it boil again or the egg will scramble.
Return the chicken, season with salt and: Return the chicken, season with salt and pepper and finish with dill.
Mix the mince with the very finely grate: Mix the mince with the very finely grated onion, salt and pepper.
Cut each wrapper into four small squares: Cut each wrapper into four small squares, put a pea-sized blob of filling in the middle and pinch the four corners together into a little parcel.
Stir the crushed garlic into the yoghurt: Stir the crushed garlic into the yoghurt and leave it at room temperature.
Boil the manti in salted water until the: Boil the manti in salted water until the pastry is tender.
Melt the butter with the chilli flakes a: Melt the butter with the chilli flakes and paprika until it foams red.
Spoon the manti into bowls, cover with t: Spoon the manti into bowls, cover with the garlic yoghurt, drizzle with the red butter and sprinkle with dried mint.
Soak the bulgur in cold water, then drai: Soak the bulgur in cold water, then drain it and squeeze it really dry.
Knead most of the mince with the bulgur,: Knead most of the mince with the bulgur, a little grated onion, the cumin, half the cinnamon, the salt and pepper into a smooth paste.
For the filling, fry the rest of the min: For the filling, fry the rest of the mince and the rest of the onion, chopped, in half the oil with the pine nuts and the rest of the cinnamon.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Press half the p: Heat the oven to 190°C. Press half the paste into an oiled dish, spread over the filling, then cover with the rest of the paste, smoothing it with wet hands.
Score a diamond pattern on top, brush wi: Score a diamond pattern on top, brush with the rest of the oil and bake until browned.
Serve with the yoghurt mixed with choppe: Serve with the yoghurt mixed with chopped cucumber and mint.
Blitz or finely chop the coriander, pars: Blitz or finely chop the coriander, parsley, garlic, cumin, paprika, lemon juice, half the oil and the salt into a green paste: this is the chermoula.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss thin potato: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss thin potato slices, sliced pepper and tomato wedges with a third of the chermoula and the rest of the oil in a baking dish, and roast.
Meanwhile, rub the rest of the chermoula: Meanwhile, rub the rest of the chermoula over the fish.
Lay the fish on the vegetables, scatter: Lay the fish on the vegetables, scatter with the olives and bake until it flakes easily.
Soften the sliced pepper and garlic in t: Soften the sliced pepper and garlic in the oil.
Stir in the harissa, paprika and cumin f: Stir in the harissa, paprika and cumin for a few seconds, then add the tomatoes and simmer into a thick, spicy sauce.
Season the fish with salt, nestle it int: Season the fish with salt, nestle it into the sauce, cover and poach gently until it flakes.
Finish with plenty of coriander and a sq: Finish with plenty of coriander and a squeeze of lemon.
Rinse the quinoa, then simmer it in twic: Rinse the quinoa, then simmer it in twice its volume of salted water until the little tails show. Drain and spread it out to cool.
Chop the cucumber, halve the tomatoes an: Chop the cucumber, halve the tomatoes and slice the red onion thinly.
Whisk the lemon juice with the oil and t: Whisk the lemon juice with the oil and toss it through the salad with the drained chickpeas, olives, parsley and mint. It keeps well for lunch the next day.
Whisk the chickpea flour with the turmer: Whisk the chickpea flour with the turmeric, cumin, salt and enough water to make a batter like single cream. Let it rest for a few minutes.
Stir in the finely chopped onion, tomato: Stir in the finely chopped onion, tomato, chilli and coriander.
Brush a non-stick pan with oil, pour in: Brush a non-stick pan with oil, pour in a ladle of batter and spread it thin. Cook until the edges lift, then flip and cook the other side. Repeat and eat them hot.
Marinate the chicken with the yoghurt, g: Marinate the chicken with the yoghurt, grated ginger and garlic, garam masala, turmeric, chopped chilli, lemon juice and salt. Longer is better, even overnight.
Slice the onion thinly and fry it slowly: Slice the onion thinly and fry it slowly in the oil until deep brown and crisp. Lift it out and keep the oil.
Warm the saffron in the milk and leave i: Warm the saffron in the milk and leave it to infuse.
Rinse the rice and boil it with the card: Rinse the rice and boil it with the cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaf in plenty of salted water until it’s only about 70% cooked, then drain.
Spread the chicken in a heavy pot with a: Spread the chicken in a heavy pot with a spoon of the onion oil. Top with half the onions, the mint and coriander, then the rice, then the saffron milk and the rest of the onions.
Seal the pot tightly (foil under the lid: Seal the pot tightly (foil under the lid helps) and cook on the lowest heat until the chicken is done and the rice is fluffy. Rest for 10 minutes before opening.
Char the aubergine whole over a gas flam: Char the aubergine whole over a gas flame or under a very hot grill, turning, until the skin is black and the inside collapses. Peel it and roughly mash the flesh.
Fry the cumin in the oil until it sizzle: Fry the cumin in the oil until it sizzles, then add the chopped onion and cook until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, chilli, turmeric: Add the garlic, ginger, chilli, turmeric and chopped tomato and cook down until jammy.
Stir in the aubergine, garam masala and: Stir in the aubergine, garam masala and salt and cook for a few minutes more. Finish with coriander and serve with the rice.
Brown the chicken pieces in half the oil: Brown the chicken pieces in half the oil on high heat, then lift them out.
Add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the: Add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the chunky onion and pepper until charred at the edges but still crunchy.
Add the garlic, ginger, sliced chilli an: Add the garlic, ginger, sliced chilli and the spices, fry for a minute, then add the chopped tomato and cook until saucy.
Return the chicken and simmer until cook: Return the chicken and simmer until cooked through. Salt to taste, finish with coriander and serve with the rice.
Mix a third of the yoghurt with the gara: Mix a third of the yoghurt with the garam masala, paprika, grated ginger and garlic, lemon juice and salt, and coat the salmon in it.
Grill or roast the salmon at the highest: Grill or roast the salmon at the highest heat until charred at the edges and just cooked in the middle.
For the raita, grate the cucumber, squee: For the raita, grate the cucumber, squeeze it and mix it with the rest of the yoghurt and chopped mint. Serve with the salmon and rice.
Heat the grill. Warm the beans with the: Heat the grill. Warm the beans with the oil and cumin, mashing them into a thick paste.
Spread the beans over the bread, cover w: Spread the beans over the bread, cover with the grated cheese and grill until melted and bubbling.
Mix the chopped tomato, onion, chilli an: Mix the chopped tomato, onion, chilli and coriander with a squeeze of lime and the salt into a pico de gallo and spoon it over.
Blend the garlic, cumin, oregano, paprik: Blend the garlic, cumin, oregano, paprika, pepper, salt, vinegar and the juice of most of the lime into a red marinade. Smoked paprika stands in for achiote.
Rub it all over the pork, cut into big c: Rub it all over the pork, cut into big chunks, and marinate for at least half an hour. Overnight is best.
Wrap the pork tightly in foil (or banana: Wrap the pork tightly in foil (or banana leaves if you have them) with all the marinade and roast at 160°C until it falls apart.
Meanwhile, pickle the thinly sliced red: Meanwhile, pickle the thinly sliced red onion with the rest of the lime juice, the sliced chilli and a pinch of salt.
Shred the pork in its juices and serve i: Shred the pork in its juices and serve it on warm tortillas with the pink onions.
Char the peppers under a hot grill or ov: Char the peppers under a hot grill or over a flame until blistered all over, then cover them in a bowl to steam. Poblanos are traditional if you can find them.
Simmer the tomatoes with the chopped oni: Simmer the tomatoes with the chopped onion, garlic, oregano and salt into a light sauce.
Peel the peppers, slit one side, pull ou: Peel the peppers, slit one side, pull out the seeds and stuff them with the cheese.
Whisk the egg white to stiff peaks, then: Whisk the egg white to stiff peaks, then fold in the yolk. Dust the peppers with flour and dip them in the egg.
Fry them in the hot oil, spooning it ove: Fry them in the hot oil, spooning it over the top, until puffed and golden. Serve in a pool of the tomato sauce with the rice.
Blend the tomatoes with the onion and ga: Blend the tomatoes with the onion and garlic until smooth.
Toast the fideo or broken thin spaghetti: Toast the fideo or broken thin spaghetti in the oil, stirring, until golden brown. This is what gives the soup its flavour.
Pour in the tomato mixture and fry it fo: Pour in the tomato mixture and fry it for a couple of minutes, then add the stock and salt and simmer until the noodles are soft.
Serve with a squeeze of lime, coriander: Serve with a squeeze of lime, coriander and a few slices of avocado.
Crisp the tortillas in a hot oven or dry: Crisp the tortillas in a hot oven or dry pan until hard and golden: now they’re tostadas.
Mix the tuna with the mayonnaise, chipot: Mix the tuna with the mayonnaise, chipotle, finely chopped red onion and half the lime juice.
Mash the avocado with the rest of the li: Mash the avocado with the rest of the lime and a pinch of salt.
Spread the avocado on the tostadas, pile: Spread the avocado on the tostadas, pile on the tuna and top with diced cucumber and coriander.
Snap the woody ends off the asparagus an: Snap the woody ends off the asparagus and cut the spears into short pieces.
Gently fry the sliced garlic in the oil,: Gently fry the sliced garlic in the oil, add the asparagus and cook until tender but still bright green.
Beat the eggs lightly with the salt and: Beat the eggs lightly with the salt and pepper, pour them in and stir slowly over low heat. Take them off while they’re still soft and glossy.
Put the chorizo, black pudding and bacon: Put the chorizo, black pudding and bacon in a pot with the halved onion, the garlic and bay leaf, cover with the stock and simmer to flavour the broth.
Add the drained beans, the saffron and t: Add the drained beans, the saffron and the paprika. White fabes are traditional; butter beans are a good stand-in.
Simmer very gently, shaking the pot inst: Simmer very gently, shaking the pot instead of stirring so the beans stay whole, until the broth is thick and orange.
Lift out the meats, slice them and serve: Lift out the meats, slice them and serve them on top of the beans. Taste before adding salt: the meats are already salty.
Season the chicken with salt and brown i: Season the chicken with salt and brown it in the oil, then take it out.
Fry the almonds and garlic in the same o: Fry the almonds and garlic in the same oil until golden, then lift them out.
Soften the chopped onion, then add the w: Soften the chopped onion, then add the wine and let it bubble for a minute.
Return the chicken with the stock and ba: Return the chicken with the stock and bay leaf and simmer, covered, until tender.
Meanwhile, hard-boil the egg and cook th: Meanwhile, hard-boil the egg and cook the rice.
Pound the almonds, garlic, saffron and e: Pound the almonds, garlic, saffron and egg yolk into a paste, stir it into the sauce to thicken it and simmer a few minutes more. Serve with the rice, topped with the chopped egg white and parsley.
